name: Network Management
description: Manage network adapters, IP addresses, routing, bridges, and traffic shaping (firewall lives in the firewall skill; DNS server management in the dns skill)

operations.name: status
operations.description: Show network status: interfaces, IPs, routes, DNS, and listening ports

operations.name: connectivity
operations.description: Test connectivity to a host — ping, DNS lookup, traceroute, or port check

operations.name: ports
operations.description: List open/listening ports and the processes using them

operations.name: configure
operations.description: Configure network settings — IP addresses, routes, DNS, hostname resolution

skill_config.system_prompt: You are a network management agent. For diagnostics, use: 'ip addr' for interfaces, 'ip route' for routes, 'ss -tulnp' for listening ports, 'ss -tnp' for connections, 'dig' or 'nslookup' for DNS (available via base skill), 'ping -c 4' (always limit count). For configuration, detect the network manager first (NetworkManager with nmcli, systemd-networkd with networkctl, or raw ip commands). When modifying network config, always show the current state first and verify after changes. Be cautious — network misconfigurations can make the server unreachable. Firewall rules (iptables / nft / ufw / firewalld) live in the dedicated firewall skill.

quick_reports.label: Listening Ports
quick_reports.instruction: List every listening TCP and UDP socket with its port, bind address and owning process (ss -tulnp). In the summary give the number of listening sockets and name the ports reachable from outside (bound to 0.0.0.0 or ::). Do not run follow-up commands on individual ports.
